summary: At the table Jesus announces that one of the Twelve will betray Him; He quietly identifies Judas with a piece of bread, and Judas goes out into the night.
key_insight: No one pointed at Judas. Each disciple asked, “Lord, is it I?” Even after Jesus handed Judas the bread and said, “What you do, do quickly,” no one at the table understood. Jesus made the truth plain to Judas without exposing him to the others.
story: As they reclined and ate, Jesus was troubled in spirit {Jn} and said, “Assuredly, I say to you, one of you who eats with Me will betray Me.” {Mk} “But behold, the hand of My betrayer is with Me on the table.” {Lk}

The disciples looked at one another, unsure whom He meant. {Jn} They were exceedingly sorrowful, {Mt} and they began to question among themselves which of them it could be. {Lk} One by one they said to Him, “Is it I?” {Mk}

He answered, “It is one of the twelve, who dips with Me in the dish. The Son of Man indeed goes just as it is written of Him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been good for that man if he had never been born.” {Mk} Then Judas, who was betraying Him, asked, “Rabbi, is it I?” Jesus said to him, “You have said it.” {Mt}

The disciple whom Jesus loved was reclining next to Him. Simon Peter motioned to him to ask who it was. So he leaned back against Jesus’ breast and said, “Lord, who is it?” Jesus answered, “It is he to whom I shall give a piece of bread when I have dipped it.” He dipped the bread and gave it to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon. {Jn}

After the piece of bread, Satan entered him. Jesus said to him, “What you do, do quickly.” No one at the table knew why He said this. Because Judas kept the money box, some thought Jesus was telling him to buy what they needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor. {Jn}
Having received the piece of bread, Judas went out immediately. “And it was night.” {Jn}
differences: Matthew and Mark place the announcement while they were eating, before the bread and cup; Luke places Jesus’ words about the betrayer’s hand after the cup (22:21).
Only Matthew records Judas’s question, “Rabbi, is it I?” and Jesus’ answer, “You have said it.”

Matthew and Mark point to the one who dips in the dish with Jesus; John tells of the piece of bread Jesus dipped and handed to Judas, the beloved disciple’s question and Judas going out into the night.
Luke says Satan entered Judas before he went to the chief priests (22:3); John says Satan entered him after the piece of bread (13:27).

fit.question: Was Judas still at the table for the Lord’s Supper? Matthew and Mark tell of the betrayer before the bread and cup, and John says Judas left right after the piece of bread. Luke records Jesus’ words about the betrayer after the cup.

points.label: Judas left before
points.text: Many hold that the piece of bread in John came during the Passover meal, before Jesus gave the bread and cup, and Judas went out at once (John 13:30). Luke often groups material by subject, and he may have gathered the sayings about the betrayer and the disciples’ failures after the Supper.

points.label: Judas stayed
points.text: Others take Luke’s order as the order of events, so Judas shared the bread and cup and left afterward. John does not describe the Supper, so his account does not settle when it came.

fit.note: The Gospels do not fix the exact moment Judas left. Each account is true to what happened, and none requires an error.
fit.short: Many think Judas left before the bread and cup; others follow Luke’s order and think he stayed. The text does not settle it.

fit.question: Luke says Satan entered Judas before he made his bargain with the chief priests (Luke 22:3). John says Satan entered him at the supper, after the piece of bread (John 13:27). Which is right?

points.label: Step by step
points.text: John himself shows a process. Before supper, the devil had already put the betrayal into Judas’s heart (13:2); at the table, Satan entered him. Luke describes Satan’s first decisive hold; John, his full grip on Judas for the deed that night.

points.label: Judas’s own choice
points.text: Neither writer excuses Judas. He went to the priests, took the money and left the table by his own will, and each step bound him more tightly.

fit.note: Both writers describe the same dark work at different moments, from the bargain to the betrayal.
fit.short: Satan prompted Judas before the bargain and took full hold of him at the supper. John himself shows both steps (13:2, 27).

scene.label: Reclining at table
scene.text: At festive meals, guests lay on couches or cushions around a low table, leaning on the left elbow with their feet stretched out behind. The disciple on Jesus’ right could lean back against His chest and speak privately, which is how the beloved disciple asked his question.

scene.label: The shared dish
scene.text: Several diners shared a bowl, dipping bread into a sauce. Jesus’ words, “one of the twelve, who dips with Me in the dish,” did not single Judas out to the others, since all of them were eating from it. They stressed how close the betrayer was.

scene.label: The piece of bread
scene.text: A host could honor a guest by dipping a morsel and handing it to him. Judas was near enough to receive it directly, perhaps in a place of honor; Edersheim thought Judas reclined at Jesus’ left. Scripture does not say.

witnesses.matthew: Alone records Judas’s own question. The others say “Lord, is it I?”; Judas says “Rabbi.” Jesus’ reply, “You have said it,” gives Judas a plain answer that the rest seem not to have grasped.
witnesses.mark: Stresses how close the betrayer was: one who eats with Jesus, one of the twelve, one who dips with Him in the dish. Mark also keeps the hard sentence that it would have been good for that man never to have been born.
witnesses.luke: Places Jesus’ word about the betrayer’s hand right after the cup of the new covenant, so the gift and the betrayal sit on the same table. He notes that the disciples questioned “among themselves,” which leads straight into their argument about who was greatest (22:24).
witnesses.john: Gives an eyewitness view from beside Jesus: His troubled spirit, the beloved disciple at His side, Peter’s signal, the dipped bread. John alone says Satan entered Judas at the table, and he ends simply: “And it was night.”

seeing.reveals: Jesus is troubled in spirit, yet fully in command. He knows the betrayer, names the Scripture being fulfilled, and still offers Judas bread from His own hand. The Son of Man goes “as it is written of Him”; no betrayal takes Him by surprise.
seeing.living: Every disciple at the table asked, “Is it I?” That is still the right question when Jesus speaks of failure: look first at your own heart, not your neighbor’s. And do not mistake nearness to Jesus’ people for faithfulness to Jesus Himself; Judas sat closer than most.
seeing.ponder: When Jesus speaks a hard word, is your first question “Is it I?” or “Who is it?”

preaching.big_idea: Jesus knew the betrayer at His table, and He still held out the bread.
outline: A troubled Lord tells the truth (21–22)
A quiet question at His side (23–26)
A final choice and a dark night (27–30)
preaching.watch_for: John’s Gospel opened with the light shining in the darkness (1:5), and Jesus has called Himself the light of the world (8:12). Judas leaves the Light at the table and walks out into the night (13:30).

title: The Betrayer Revealed
